- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, reduce forecasted peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, cap the overshoot and apply mild downward correction in next 3–5 days.  
- When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (especially after a spike), assume model overreacted — apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7–14 day average.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid false bullish momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days of forecast are consistently higher than true outcome, apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to early period.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may be overfitting — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×recent + 0.3×prior) for next forecast.  
- When true outcome is below 70.00 and forecast is above 72.00, assume model is ignoring bearish sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
